statement: Qualified small business stock must be stock in a C corporation acquired by the taxpayer at original issuance (directly or through an underwriter) in exchange for money, property other than stock, or as compensation for services to the corporation (26 U.S.C. § 1202(c)); the corporation's aggregate gross assets must not exceed $50,000,000 at all times before and immediately after issuance — $75,000,000, indexed after 2026, for stock issued after July 4, 2025 (§ 1202(d)(1)); and during substantially all the holding period the corporation must meet the active business requirement (at least 80% by value of assets used in the active conduct of one or more qualified trades or businesses, § 1202(e)), which excludes services in health, law, engineering, architecture, accounting, actuarial science, performing arts, consulting, athletics, financial services, and brokerage, businesses whose principal asset is employee reputation or skill, banking/insurance/financing/leasing/investing, farming, § 613/613A extraction, and hotels, motels, and restaurants (§ 1202(e)(3)).
caveat: Redemption rules (§ 1202(c)(3)), working-capital limits, SSBIC rules, aggregation, and whether a given company's facts satisfy the active-business and excluded-field tests are legal determinations — every condition returns needs_review where facts decide. The 2025 amendments apply by issuance date; verify current law and the issuance-date regime before relying on any threshold.
